candidates.reason: It assumes Summable (fourierCoeff f); the canonical target quantifies over every continuous f without coefficient summability. It sums a bilateral Int series rather than directly proving convergence of the frozen symmetric Cesaro means.
It requires the averaged sequence u itself to converge. Fejer's theorem cannot assume convergence of the Fourier partial sums it is meant to Cesaro-sum.

The theorem is L1 convergence of a convolution on the fixed circle AddCircle (2*pi), scaled to (2*pi) * hf.toL1. It is not uniform convergence of frozen symmetric Fourier Cesaro sums for arbitrary positive period and continuous f. The file also contains a sorry-backed auxiliary declaration and fails under this repository's pinned Lean/mathlib environment.
